rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.1 / ESMA-262 6th Ed. 20.1.3.6 Number.prototype.toString — signed zero preserved
divergence_trap: JSON.stringify(-0) → "0" (drops sign) in many engines; JCS mandates "-0"

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.1 — parse to JSON data model value then re-serialize; precision loss on parse is irreversible
divergence_trap: Naive string-preserving impl outputs "9007199254740993" (the original lexical token); JCS uses the parsed IEEE 754 value

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.1 / ES6 Number.prototype.toString 'Shortest' decimal algorithm — uses exponent notation at 10^21 boundary
divergence_trap: JSON.stringify outputs "100000000000000000000" (long decimal); JCS uses exponent form

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.1 / ES6 Number.prototype.toString 'Shortest' decimal — chooses exponent form over long decimal
divergence_trap: JSON.stringify outputs "0.0000001"; JCS prefers shorter exponent form "1e-7"

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.2 — string escaping; backslash is U+005C; input had \u005C (escaped backslash), parsed as literal backslash; canonical form uses JSON-escaped form \\
divergence_trap: Impl that copies original escape sequence verbatim keeps \u005C; JCS normalizes to \\ (backslash-escaped backslash)

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.2 — solidus may be escaped as \/ but canonical form uses shortest representation (unescaped)
divergence_trap: JSON.stringify always escapes solidus as \/; JCS canonical form is unescaped /

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.2 — control chars U+0000..U+001F serialized as \u00XX hex escapes; JSON.stringify may use shorthand \n \t etc.
divergence_trap: JSON.stringify may output \t\n for the same logical string; JCS canonical uses \u0009\u000A (byte-equivalent but textual divergence)

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.2.2 / Section 3 — no Unicode normalization applied; surrogate pairs (emoji U+1F600) preserved as UTF-8 code units; no transformation
divergence_trap: Impl applying NFKC/NFKC normalization would alter or invalidate the surrogate pair; JCS explicitly does not normalize

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.1 — no whitespace; Section 4.3 — object members sorted by name; this vector verifies nesting preserves structure (same-order keys happen to be sorted already)
divergence_trap: Any whitespace injection or key reordering (if keys differed) would diverge; for this specific input, JSON.stringify produces same output but structure is verified

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4 — JCS canonical form does not exist for JSON with duplicate names; duplicate-key JSON is not valid canonical JSON
divergence_trap: Some parsers accept last-value-wins; others error; JCS has no canonical output — this vector verifies the impl correctly rejects or produces null rather than silently accepting

rule: RFC 8785 Section 4.3 — object member names sorted by UTF-16 code unit values (ES6 6.1.6.1 String). U+FDD0 = 0xFDD0; U+1F600 first surrogate 0xD83D. 0xD8 < 0xFD so emoji (surrogate-leading) sorts before nonchar in UTF-16. Code-point order (U+FDD0=64976 < U+1F600=128512) would reverse this.
divergence_trap: Impls sorting by Unicode code point order (e.g. Python json, naive UTF-8 byte sort) output {"\uFDD0":1,"\uD83D\uDE00":2}; JCS UTF-16 code unit sort outputs emoji first
